title: Fix layered serving-defaults precedence causing customer eval divergence
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Customer KeyCo reported a sudden divergence in offline eval scores and production prompt outputs after the runtime-1.24 rollout. Symptoms: higher token counts, trailing chat artifacts, and deterministic eval failures vs their baseline. Initial triage indicated the change correlated with a rollout that adjusted the default sampling profile and introduced a new layered config inheritance model (global hosted defaults -> dedicated pool profile -> customer pinned overrides). The suspected root cause is a precedence bug: when a customer had explicit stop-sequence overrides in Private deployments, the serving layer incorrectly preferred the Dedicated pool's sampling profile and a legacy stop mapping, effectively stripping the customer override in some request paths. This caused sampling temperature and stop-seq behavior to differ between environments (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) and between direct API calls and routed requests, resulting in measurable eval regressions for KeyCo's test suite. This ticket scopes investigation, reproduce, hotfix, rollout, and verification across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments. Work items: 1) Reproduce with KeyCo prompt suite and our internal eval harness across all deployment types. 2) Implement fix in config resolution ordering in the runtime: ensure customer-pinned overrides always win, then pool profile, then global default. 3) Add unit and integration tests to cover all combinations including edge-case empty/NULL stop arrays and header-based routing fallthrough. 4) Backport hotfix to 1.24 and create migration plan for active Dedicated pools. 5) Run coordinated rollout and monitor KeyCo and system-wide evals for parity. 6) Postmortem and product/Docs updates explaining precedence model.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Ava Martinez: Received escalation from Customer Success (KeyCo). Initial customer examples attached. Marked as P0 due to production eval regressions impacting SLAs.

2026-03-02 - Rohan Patel: Reproduced divergence locally with KeyCo's prompt set. Observed that Private deployment container returned different stop tokens than Hosted for identical request payloads. Started grep through config resolution codepath.

2026-03-03 - Marcus Green: Found a conditional in config_merger.go where poolProfile != nil branch executed after customerOverrides merge, effectively shadowing customer stop-seq when poolProfile had non-empty sampling profile. Added unit test scaffolding to capture this case.

2026-03-04 - Rohan Patel: Submitted draft PR fixing precedence (github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1324). PR includes new integration test that simulates header-based routing and private-pool pinning. Requesting expedited review.

2026-03-05 - Leah Chen (SRE): Ran canary in staging with hotfix patch; KeyCo baseline eval now matches expected output for 95% of tests. Two flakey tests remain related to deterministic seeding; digging in.
2026-03-08 - Product (Priya Kulkarni): Notified KeyCo of in-flight fix and requested permission to run production canary on a 5% traffic slice for their tenant. Customer approved with conditions.

2026-03-10 - Rohan Patel: Hotfix merged to main and cherry-picked to release/runtime-1.24-hotfix branch. Deployment runbooks updated. Observability dashboard tile added to console for per-customer stop-seq parity.

2026-03-12 - Ava Martinez: Monitoring shows KeyCo production eval match rate moved from 78% -> 99% after canary. Closing immediate escalation on customer side; keeping ticket open for postmortem and broader regression guardrails.

Follow-ups: add e2e tests to CI that exercise (Hosted, Dedicated, Private) cross-checks; release a short FAQ for customers about precedence semantics; consider telemetry to surface silent stop-seq drops.
